record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: For natural classes of mathematical structures, such as ordered sets and relatively free algebras, and for subsemigroups of their endomorphism semigroups, determine: (1) which subclasses are defined up to isomorphism by these semigroups; and (2) which subsemigroups of endomorphism semigroups determine the structures up to isomorphism.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.13. (E.S. Lyapin) For natural classes of mathematical structures - such as ordered
sets, relatively free algebras, and for subsemigroups of endomorphism semigroups of these structures
- determine:

     (1) Subclasses of structures defined up to isomorphism by these semigroups;
     (2) Subsemigroups of endomorphism semigroups that determine these structures up to isomor-
         phism.

For various classes of partially ordered sets E.S. Lyapin found endomorphism semigroups that
determine these classes up to isomorphism (see [11], [12], [13]).

          For a mathematical structure A, denote by End(A) (respectively Aut(A)) the semigroup
(respectively group) of its endomorphisms (automorphisms) under composition. The sequence

                  End(A), End(End(A)), . . .   (respectively Aut(A), Aut(Aut(A)), . . .)

is called the tower of endomorphisms (respectively tower of automorphisms) of A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a mathematical structure $A$ (for example, a partially ordered set, a relatively free algebra, or another algebraic or relational structure), let $\mathrm{End}(A)$ denote the semigroup of all endomorphisms of $A$ under composition, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(A)$ denote the group of all automorphisms of $A$. A class $\mathcal{K}$ of structures is said to be determined up to isomorphism by endomorphism semigroups if, for any $A,B\in\mathcal{K}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{End}(A)\cong\mathrm{End}(B)$ of semigroups implies $A\cong B$. More generally, given an assignment that to each structure $A$ associates a subsemigroup $S(A)\subseteq\mathrm{End}(A)$, the structures in $\mathcal{K}$ are said to be determined up to isomorphism by $S$ if $S(A)\cong S(B)$ as semigroups implies $A\cong B$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{K}$.

For natural classes of mathematical structures — in particular, classes of ordered sets and classes of relatively free algebras — solve the following two problems:

(1) Identify those subclasses $\mathcal{K}$ that are determined up to isomorphism by their endomorphism semigroups $\mathrm{End}(A)$, $A\in\mathcal{K}$.

(2) Identify those distinguished subsemigroups $S(A)\subseteq\mathrm{End}(A)$ (defined uniformly across the class) such that the assignment $A\mapsto S(A)$ determines the structures of $\mathcal{K}$ up to isomorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broadly stated research program of Lyapin on the recovery of structures from their endomorphism semigroups. While many partial results exist (for various classes of partially ordered sets and algebraic structures, endomorphism semigroups have been shown to determine the structure up to isomorphism — work by Lyapin and many subsequent authors on monoids of endomorphisms of algebras, lattices, ordered sets, etc.), no general resolution covering all "natural classes" exists, and the problem is recorded as still being a guiding open research direction.
